title: Pitney Bowes Announces Date for Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Release and Conference Call
summary: SHELTON, Conn. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 16, 2026-- Pitney Bowes Inc. (NYSE: PBI), a technology-driven products and services company that provides digital shipping solutions, mailing innovation, and financial services to clients around the world – including more than 90 percent of the Fortune 500 –
body_text: News & Highlights News & Press Releases Presentations Events Sign up for Alerts View printer-friendly version << Back Pitney Bowes Announces Date for Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Release and Conference Call SHELTON, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 16, 2026-- Pitney Bowes Inc. (NYSE: PBI), a technology-driven products and services company that provides digital shipping solutions, mailing innovation, and financial services to clients around the world – including more than 90 percent of the Fortune 500 – today announced that it will report second quarter 2026 earnings results after market close on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. The Company will host an investor conference call the next day on Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. ET to review its results. Small businesses to large enterprises, and government entities rely on Pitney Bowes to reduce the complexity of sending mail and parcels. title: Tuya Smart to Showcase Outdoor IoT and Cellular Connectivity Technology at 2022 Mobile World Congress | news | Tuya Smart
body_text: Tuya Smart ("Tuya" or the "Company") (NYSE: TUYA), a global IoT development platform service provider, today announced it will attend the 2022 Mobile World Congress (MWC) in Barcelona, Spain. The Company plans to showcase its cellular connectivity products and demonstrate how Tuya Smart supports the advancement of outdoor IoT devices through cellular connectivity capabilities. At this year’s MWC in Barcelona, running from February 28 until March 3, Tuya Smart will showcase its comprehensive suite of cellular connectivity capabilities to thousands of visitors. This year’s MWC theme, “One Step Closer to the Smart Life,” reflects the progress the Company has made in supporting the expansion of the outdoor IoT technology industry, including strengthening device the accuracy, features and distances covered. While IoT devices were previously restricted to indoor and smart home scenarios, devices have gradually expanded to short-range and mid-range outdoor solutions, backed by Wi-Fi, Zigbee, and Bluetooth technology. And increasingly developers are in search of solutions beyond the normal medium and short-range communication protocols. Tuya Smart offers a comprehensive suite of hardware and software solutions for short, medium, and long distance outdoor IoT product development, such as LTE Cat.1, NB-IoT and other long-range cellular communication protocols. Tuya’s thriving ecosystem currently provides hardware and software support for a large portfolio of outdoor products including smart scooters and smart mobility, smart trackers, smart energy, outdoor lighting, industry, and agriculture. Tuya’s powerful platform development tools include the development of OEM apps, globally deployed cloud services and various network modules. The Company’s cloud services also support important features for outdoor scenarios, such as device positioning, geofencing, route tracking, and other energy efficient solutions to support device mobility and a strong travel experience to users. For electric scooters and other outdoor travel applications, Tuya has tailored the support of key features such as real-time tracking of device battery or remaining ride distance for electric vehicles or scooters, to help users accurately plan their route and device charging. For shared electric scooters or power banks, Tuya Smart’s tools also support business developers in accurately tracking fleet location, charging station status and in managing the device pool. Tuya Smart continues to expand its outdoor communication tools to help developers provide cutting-edge products for business and customers uses. As of September 30, 2021, the Tuya IoT development platform served over 446,000 developers around the world, with its IoT PaaS empowering over 3,800 brands to develop smart devices including Calex, Philips, Schneider Electric and more. As new mobility and outdoor applications for IoT continue to grow, Tuya Smart will support its thriving ecosystem of developers, OEMs and brands to build comprehensive products. About Tuya Smart Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA) is a leading technology company focused on making our lives smarter. Tuya does this through offering a cloud platform that connects a range of devices via the IoT. By building interconnectivity standards, Tuya bridges the intelligent needs of brands, OEMs, developers, and retail chains across a broad range of smart devices and industries. Tuya solutions empower partners and customers by improving the value of their products while making consumers’ lives more convenient through the application of technology. Through its growing commercial SaaS business, Tuya offers intelligent business solutions for a wide range of verticals. The Company’s platform is backed by industry-leading technology complete with rigorous data protection and security. Tuya partners with leading Fortune 500 companies from around the world to make things smarter, including Philips, Schneider Electric, Lenovo and many others.

title: GetAccept earns spot on G2’s 2023 Best Software Awards for Sales Products
summary: GetAccept earns top spot on G2's 2023 best software awards for sales products, and is the highest rated digital sales room and electronic signature tool.
body_text: Palo Alto, CA - February 8, 2023 – GetAccept, the Digital Sales Room platform, today announced it has been named to G2’s 2023 Best Software Awards , placing 11th on the Sales Product list. As the world’s largest and most trusted software marketplace, G2 is visited by 80 million software buyers each year. Its annual Best Software Awards rank the world’s best software companies and products based on authentic, timely reviews from real users . This is GetAccept ’s first time receiving a G2’s Best Software Award recognition, earning its place this year thanks to their mission to radically redefine the way companies run sales. GetAccept’s Digital Sales Room empowers revenue teams to increase win rates by engaging and understanding buyers from opportunity to signed deal, removing friction and at the same time increasing engagement in the buying process. The platform leverages sales content management, proposals and contracts, CPQ, tracking and analytics, mutual action plans, electronic signatures, and seamlessly integrates with your CRM, instantly updating all interactions in one place: the Digital Sales Room. “We’re so proud to be named to G2’s 2023 Best Software Awards, ranking on the Sales Product list, together with other companies that we admire” says Samir Smajic, GetAccept’s CEO and co-founder. “The GetAccept Digital Sales Room platform is designed to provide a complete digital selling and buying experience in one engaging shared space. The software buying journey is very complex today and we’re honored to be part of this award showing that we are committed to making a difference for B2B buyers everywhere.” “While G2 publishes the Best Software Awards each year, they’re really awards from customers,” said Sara Rossio, Chief Product Officer at G2. “Representing a vote of confidence from real software users, these awards also spotlight those that have risen to the top among thousands of companies. With 2 million+ verified software reviews, the most in a single destination, our marketplace features more than 145,000 products and services across 2,100 different categories. Congratulations to all those named, as buyers will continue to lean on these awards as a trusted source to inform their software decisions in the year ahead.” The top 100 companies are ranked based on a combination of Satisfaction and Market Presence scores for each vendor, and the top 100 products are ranked based on reviews across all categories they are a part of. To be recognized as a Best Software Award winner, a software company or product must receive at least 50 approved and published reviews during the 2022 calendar year. Scores reflect only data from reviews submitted during this evaluation period. To learn more, view G2’s 2023 Best Software Awards and read more about G2’s methodology . About G2 G2 is the world's largest and most trusted software marketplace. More than 80 million people annually — including employees at all Fortune 500 companies — use G2 to make smarter software decisions based on authentic peer reviews. Thousands of software and services companies of all sizes partner with G2 to build their reputation, manage their software spend, and grow their business — including Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoom, and Adobe. To learn more about where you go for software, visit www.g2.com and follow us on Twitter and LinkedIn . About GetAccept From start-up challenger in 2015 to becoming an industry leader, GetAccept is radically redefining the way companies run sales. Providing a Digital Sales platform that empowers revenue teams to increase their win rates by engaging and understanding buyers from opportunity to signed deal. Buyers and sellers can interact in one shared space, sharing sales content, mutual action plans, proposals and quotes, contracts and e-sign documents throughout the sales process. Integrates seamlessly with your CRM, instantly updating all interactions in the digital sales room, providing real-time insights about active deals, enabling sales teams to keep track of the true pipeline and maximize performance with the help of tracking, analytics, smart reminders and advanced reporting. Swedish entrepreneurs and Y Combinator alumni Samir Smajic, Mathias Thulin, Jonas Blanck, and Carl Carell founded GetAccept in 2015. The platform serves 40,000+ users across 4,000+ enterprises within 60+ countries. GetAccept is headquartered in Malmö, Sweden and has a team of 200+ employees across the US, Sweden, United Kingdom, France, Norway, and Denmark. title: Loyalty Unpacked – United Airlines
summary: Inside MileagePlus, miles meet cards & media. The NALA™ examines its business model in Loyalty Unpacked United Airlines for frequent flyers.
body_text: United MileagePlus, the loyalty program once valued at $21.9 billion, more than the airline that owns it. The program runs as its own business inside United: most mile sales go to partners, led by the co-brand bank, and since 2024 Kinective Media sells advertising across nearly 100,000 seatback screens and 110 million traveler profiles, with free Starlink Wi-Fi as the login. In April 2026 the logic reversed. The card now sets the earn rate, and a member without one earns 40% fewer miles on the same fare. The move is financially coherent, and frequent flyers read it as a devaluation. If they stop flying, why keep the airline card? DOWNLOAD FULL PDF HERE Loyalty Unpacked ™️ is NALA’s independent content series exploring some of North America’s most recognised loyalty programs. Rather than reviewing features or scoring, we examine the commercial thinking behind programs, the problems they’re trying to solve and the questions they raise. Each edition offers practical observations, honest challenges and a NALA Insight ™️ designed to help loyalty, CRM and customer engagement teams think differently about the decisions shaping modern loyalty.

title: Legal Services Firm Returns to Reliable HR and Payroll Solution
summary: See how a legal services firm returned to CBIZ for a reliable HR and payroll solution after a low-cost switch left them without dependable support.
body_text: Issue This client, a legal services firm, initially transitioned away from CBIZ in 2024 after being presented with a seemingly lower-cost HR and payroll solution from Paychex. Shortly after making the switch, the client realized the new platform did not meet expectations and could not deliver both strong technology and reliable HR support. The client experienced limited access to support, frequent ticket submissions, delayed responses, and a lack of continuity between service teams. As a result, they swiftly considered returning to CBIZ. Solution As the client considered transitioning back to CBIZ, our payroll and HR teams: Maintained a proactive and relationship-driven approach. Stayed engaged with the client through consistent, coordinated outreach. Provided clear comparisons between Paychex and CBIZ payroll and HR service offerings, helping the client better understand the differences in value, service, and outcomes. Aligned pricing with the client’s previous arrangement to help facilitate return. Retained the same HR Services team, providing continuity, and leveraged their existing knowledge of the client’s employees, processes, and business needs. Utilized the client’s previous HCM platform setup and established system configurations where possible, allowing for a more efficient implementation and a seamless transition back to CBIZ. Leveraging the client’s positive past experiences with CBIZ, the team positioned a streamlined return to a comprehensive, trusted solution. Outcome Within a year, the client chose to return to CBIZ, reimplementing the HCM platform and reestablishing outsourced HR support. The transition resulted in improved operational efficiency and a more cohesive HR and payroll experience. By restoring a familiar and effective solution backed by responsive service, CBIZ helped the client regain confidence and stabilize internal processes, strengthening a long-term partnership once again. The client benefited from improved response times and direct access to dedicated team members who understood their business, reinforcing the value of personalized service over a lower-cost alternative. title: Markets on Beanstalk Call Notes
summary: Notes on how to prioritize the rollout of Beanstalk-native markets.
body_text: From January to March 2023, Beanstalk developers conducted public calls each week discussing design, development and roadmap decisions (these calls are now held on an ad hoc basis). These discussions are a chance for high level coordination and transparent decision making with regards to the many engineering challenges involved in creating a robust decentralized and censorship resistant financial tech stack. On February 28th, developers discussed the implementation of Beanstalk native assets as ERC-1155s, the expansion of the Pod Market to allow for the exchange of Silo Deposits, and Stalk and Seed liquidity. This post is a set of notes from the discussion. Discussion Conclusions Next steps are to implement Silo Deposits and Plots as ERC-1155s. The first market to be built should allow the exchange of Silo Deposits and Plots, with the ability to trade against ERC-20s added later. Stalk per BDV will not be included at first, due to the complexities involved. Stalk and Seeds are not required to be liquid at first, but can be added later. Pod Marketplace Context There is some inefficiency in the secondary market for Beanstalk debt. V1 of the Pod Marketplace facilitated the sale of Plots for Beans, which was not previously possible because Pods do not implement any ERC standard and thus there was no way to exchange Pods in a permissionless setting. You could list a Plot for a given amount of Beans or place an order with Beans for some Pods. Because Pods are ordered, an order includes a parameter for Place in Line. Statically priced orders result in some inefficiency. V2 supported polynomial functions, implementing a pricing curve, where price is a function of place in line. Currently there is no UI supporting it. V3 could offer Silo Deposits or Fertilizer for Pods. Placing orders with Deposits has the advantage that the user wouldn't have to forfeit all the Stalk and potential Bean seignorage accrued while the Beans are in an order. Something like Tractor or Seaport would provide the ability to place orders for arbitrary assets against arbitrary assets, such as if Deposits or Pods were to be implemented as ERC-1155s. The orders could still be a function of place in line as with V2, preserving those efficiency gains. Benefits of Seaport/Tractor Tractor and Seaport facilitate off-chain orders which can be significantly more complex with less on-chain development, but which are particularly complicated to support at the UI level. There are a lot of open questions around creating a user interface that can support whatever pairs are made available. The difficulty is underscored by the fact that there is still no V2 UI. Part of this conversation is an attempt to prioritize markets that could be built on Tractor/Seaport. Which exchanges are in Beanstalk's interest to facilitate? There may be some value in offering many different pairs, but that will fragment liquidity and require a very sophisticated aggregator. An advantage of Tractor/Seaport is that you can have asynchronous orders created and stored off-chain, and you can have the execution of an order affect the status of other orders. This makes liquidity much more efficient, but also introduces significant complexity at the indexer and UI level. Pod Orders for Tokens Already possible on the back end. You can create one massive order that will accept a variety of tokens and references an oracle that is included in the order, and allow a user to buy with any combination of tokens. Encoding one large order is harder for the indexer to process, because it would have to assess each asset and calculate the price of each using some oracle. An alternative would be to create multiple different orders, one each for all the acceptable currencies. The downside to that is the from the user experience perspective, where the user would have to sign to authorize multiple transactions. With Tractor, it may be possible to sign a list of orders at once, which would improve the user experience. In either case, it's mostly already possible to do either on the back end, the more significant challenges are the indexer and UI. The less custom functionality the better in that respect. The indexer will need to be able to code every single function selector that's used, so minimizing the set of possibilities makes the indexing task simpler. Users might desire to denominate their desired price in stable currency, so you'd have to specify some oracle price. This is ultimately one of the biggest issues as you support multiple tokens. The UI should be able to make a determination which order offers the best price in practice given the starting currency. As much as possible should be abstracted away from the user. Especially if used in combination with Pipeline, the possibilities can be infinite, so narrowing the scope to just a few currencies would probably make it easier overall. It's much more straightforward for a seller to create a listing that specifies which currency he is accepting and have the buyer perform the conversion as part of the sale, versus encoding the conversion as part of the sell order. It's a matter of how complex to make things from an SDK/UI perspective. The goal is obviously to enable any user to fill any open order in one transaction. Which Trading Pairs Make Sense? Which pairs would be economically beneficial to Beanstalk? Deposited Beans for Pods makes a lot of sense intuitively. Harder to see how a seller accepting only USDC benefits Beanstalk directly. The more assets that are accepted, the more liquid Pods become. For simplicity, it might make sense to start with just Beans and then expand to whitelisted assets (assets that have implicit value to Beanstalk). From a UI perspective, the cost of adding tradeable assets depends largely on how complicated the UI will be to begin with. A simple UI can accommodate more assets easily than a more involved UI. Different asset types (ERC-20/721/1155) will greatly increase the complexity of the UI, so constraining those would make a lot of sense. Implementing Bean deposits and Pods as ERC-1155 may make marketplaces easier to support rather than having to develop two new interfaces for one that talks to deposits and one that talks to Pods. Supporting 1155s against 1155s from a UI perspective will be difficult. Even 1155s to arbitrary 20s is a lot easier than 1155s to 1155s. A simple interface for exchanging Deposits and Pods as ERC-1155s can be done. But one that enables efficient pricing will be much more difficult. Pods change in value depending on place in line, and Deposits differ based on season. It's not clear how to display that in a digestible way to let somebody discover the right pricing. When both assets are semi-fungible, it may inherently fragment liquidity. Ideally, Deposits themselves could be abstracted and flattened such that orders can start being only two dimensional on the Deposit side. The way to get around this fragmentation might be through Stalk liquidity. It's important for the BDV of Silo Deposits and the Bean ERC-20 token to be highly interchangeable. There are numerous ways to do this from an interface perspective. It's desirable to be able abstract away as much as possible. The improvements to the Pod Marketplace are going to open up a lot of liquidity in the form of Bean and BEAN:3CRV Deposits, and users with Beans should be able to access all of that liquidity. Seems like being able to trade Deposits for Pods is complicated but obviously economically beneficial to Beanstalk. You probably have to have Stalk liquidity before the market can become particularly efficient or abstract from a user perspective. You could in theory have a Deposits for Pods marketplace with no consideration of Stalk whatsoever, which would be a minor upgrade from the current Pod marketplace, but not up to par with the full functionality. There's a lot of unanswered questions around how to facilitate the most efficient and abstract interaction with the different axes of Deposits. Other Markets In addition to Pods and Deposits, some sort of Bean Deposit future where there is forward looking expected yield priced into current BDV is an interesting Market to consider. Probably makes sense to have full spot markets before moving to derivatives. Fertilizer markets are worth considering. In theory when Stalk is liquid there will be the Deposits, which will be 1155 and are effectively the right to burn a certain amount of Stalk and Seeds with the Deposit to receive the underlying, an ERC-20 Stalk, and then some sort of semi-fungible Seed where the Seeds are yielding Stalk based on the underlying asset that is deposited. There is some work being done to further abstract the concept of Seeds, but at least with regards to Stalk and Deposits, there should be the opportunity to exchange Asset A for Stalk or Asset A for Deposits and those are distinct once you have Stalk liquid. Does It Make Sense To Have a Market That Trades Deposits Before Stalk Is Liquid? The major use case for Deposits will be people willing to buy Pods with a Deposit, and the Deposits used will be known ahead of time. So it does allow for users to make decisions about how to value the Grown Stalk. The smart contract won't necessarily need to make assumptions about the Grown Stalk. There might be value in the short term for people to be able to buy and sell Unripe Deposits on the marketplace. These markets aren't going to be fully efficient until Stalk is liquid, but there is likely still plenty of utility to be realized by enabling users to create buy orders for Plots with Deposits. Once deposits implement ERC-1155, they can also be made available on OpenSea, just without the advantage of any sort of pricing function or the ability to use Bean, and users will have to pay fees. Further Questions Facilitating Deposits on the marketplace even just as ERC-20s (including Unripe assets), and potentially also Deposits for Pods, seems to be the highest leverage. After that the question is around Stalk and potentially Seed liquidity and how that fits into everything. Should Stalk be divided into governance tokens and seignorage/interest tokens? What's the best way to facilitate efficient markets around Beanstalk? How does everything fit into the overall timeline? Which markets should roll out first? How does the liquidity around Stalk and Seeds affect the creation of markets for Deposits and does one need to happen before the other? Priorities One interesting angle is that before Stalk is liquid, Stalk per BDV is really a bonus because the Deposits come with the Stalk. Whereas after Stalk is liquid, it is really a penalty because the Deposits do not necessarily come with the Stalk. That leads to some additional complexity on the UI front. It might be necessary to develop a market that facilitates the transfer of Deposits both with and without Stalk and Seeds, depending on user preference. Starting with ERC-1155 Deposits and then later adding liquid Stalk would not change much from a UI perspective, but it would require changes to the order structure and aggregation. It may make less sense to start thinking about Stalk liquidity because it adds another degree of dimensionality, which is pretty tricky to solve from a UX standpoint. If the immediate goal is to be able to exchange Deposits, it might be a good idea to focus on that and put Stalk liquidity on the back burner until it's more clear that the market requires it. In addition, the development of liquid Stalk is quite complex and will probably be a multi-month endeavor from the point that development starts in earnest. So in the short or medium term the starting point should just be around a basic implementation of Deposits without Stalk and Seed liquidity as an 1155. This could be done in parallel with the development of Pods as 1155. The consensus seems to be to start with a Deposit for Pod marketplace and then add the Stalk functionality after the initial launch of the market. None of this needs to include the complexity of Stalk for BDV, but that can ultimately be added at the UI level at some point.

title: Oracle تفتتح ثاني مركز للبحث والتطوير في المغرب لدعم مستقبل الذكاء الاصطناعي
summary: سيساهم مركز أكادير في تطوير تقنيات السحابة والذكاء الاصطناعي لفائدة عملاء Oracle عبر العالم
body_text: أكادير، المغرب—‫30 يونيو, 2026‬ أكادير Oracle اليوم عن افتتاح ثاني مركز لها للبحث والتطوير في المغرب، في خطوة توسّع من خلالها استثماراتها داخل المنظومة التكنولوجية الوطنية، وتؤكد التزامها بتطوير تقنيات سحابية وتقنيات ذكاء اصطناعي بمواصفات عالمية، انطلاقاً من المغرب ولفائدة الأسواق الدولية. ويقع المركز الجديد بمدينة أكادير، ويأتي امتداداً للإطلاق الأخير لمركز Oracle للبحث والتطوير في الدار البيضاء، كما يشكل محطة إضافية في مسار رؤية Oracle الهادفة إلى الإسهام في ترسيخ مكانة المغرب كمركز رائد للابتكار الرقمي. وقد جرى تدشين مركز البحث والتطوير الجديد بحضور السيد عزيز أخنوش، رئيس حكومة المملكة المغربية، والسيدة أمل الفلاح السغروشني، الوزيرة المنتدبة المكلفة بالانتقال الرقمي وإصلاح الإدارة، والسيد كريم زيدان، الوزير المنتدب المكلف بالاستثمار والالتقائية وتقييم السياسات العمومية، إلى جانب سيمون دي مونتفورت ووكر، نائب الرئيس التنفيذي لتطبيقات القطاعات في Oracle. وقال السيد عزيز أخنوش: «من خلال هذا المركز الجديد للبحث والتطوير في أكادير، اختارت Oracle أن تواصل حضورها في المغرب وأن تعززه. وهذا يؤكد أن بلادنا أصبحت اليوم تحظى بالاعتراف كمنصة موثوقة وتنافسية وجذابة لأنشطة البحث والتطوير والتقنيات المتقدمة. كما يتوفر المغرب على رصيد مهم من الكفاءات عالية المستوى، وعلى مؤسسات أكاديمية قوية، وعلى طموح رقمي تقوده أعلى مستويات الدولة. ومن خلال توسيع عملياتها في المغرب، والاستثمار في مواهبنا الشابة، وإرساء قدراتها في مجال البنية التحتية السحابية، تضطلع Oracle بدور فعال باعتبارها شريكاً اقتصادياً واستراتيجياً في مسار التحول الرقمي للمملكة». ويعزز إطلاق مركز البحث والتطوير في أكادير موقع Oracle الريادي في المغرب وشمال إفريقيا. فمع دخول منطقة Oracle السحابية في الدار البيضاء حيز التشغيل، والتخطيط لإطلاق منطقة سحابية ثانية في سطات، إلى جانب وجود مركزين للبحث والتطوير في كل من الدار البيضاء وأكادير، تعمل Oracle على بناء منظومة متكاملة وغير مسبوقة في مجالي السحابة والذكاء الاصطناعي داخل المملكة. وباعتبارها المزوّد السحابي العالمي الوحيد الذي يجمع في المغرب بين البنية التحتية السحابية السيادية، والابتكار في الذكاء الاصطناعي، والبحث والتطوير المتقدمين، والاستثمار واسع النطاق في الكفاءات، تساهم Oracle في تعزيز تموقع المغرب كمركز إقليمي للابتكار في مجال الذكاء الاصطناعي. وقالت السيدة أمل الفلاح السغروشني، الوزيرة المنتدبة المكلفة بالانتقال الرقمي وإصلاح الإدارة : «إن إحداث هذا المركز الجديد للبحث والتطوير التابع لOracle في أكادير يعكس الجاذبية المتنامية لجميع جهات المغرب بالنسبة للاستثمارات التكنولوجية ذات القيمة المضافة العالية. وينسجم هذا المشروع بشكل كامل مع خارطة الطريق الوطنية “الذكاء الاصطناعي صنع في المغرب”، إذ يساهم في تطوير حلول مبتكرة في مجالات الذكاء الاصطناعي والحوسبة السحابية ومنصات البيانات، مع الاستناد إلى تميز الكفاءات المغربية. كما يبرز قدرة المملكة على استقطاب الاستثمارات الاستراتيجية، وتحفيز الابتكار، وتعزيز موقعها كمركز رقمي رائد يربط بين إفريقيا وأوروبا والشرق الأوسط». وقال السيد كريم زيدان، الوزير المنتدب المكلف بالاستثمار والالتقائية وتقييم السياسات العمومية : «إن تدشين مركز Oracle للبحث والتطوير في أكادير يبرز الجاذبية المتزايدة لجهاتنا كوجهات للاستثمار التكنولوجي عالي القيمة. فإلى جانب الدار البيضاء، بدأت مدن مختلفة عبر المملكة تبرز كمراكز للابتكار والكفاءات والتميز الرقمي، بما يعكس التزام المغرب بتنمية ترابية متوازنة وببيئة استثمارية تنافسية. وسيفتح هذا المركز الجديد آفاقاً واعدة أمام الكفاءات المغربية عالية التأهيل، كما سيقوي منظومات الابتكار الجهوية، ويعزز مكانة المغرب كوجهة استراتيجية في مجالات الذكاء الاصطناعي والتقنيات السحابية والبحث المتقدم الموجه لخدمة الأسواق العالمية». وسيركز مركز البحث والتطوير في أكادير على دفع الابتكار في عدد من المجالات، من بينها Oracle Cloud Infrastructure ، والتطبيقات المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي، ومنصات البيانات، والحلول الموجهة لمختلف القطاعات. كما سيفتح المركز فرصاً جديدة أمام المهندسين والمطورين والباحثين المغاربة ذوي الكفاءات العالية. وسيكمل هذا المركز الجديد عمليات Oracle في الدار البيضاء، بما يرسخ شبكة ابتكار متعددة المدن، تتيح تعاوناً أوسع، وتوسع قاعدة الوصول إلى المواهب، وتدعم موقع المغرب كوجهة تكنولوجية رائدة بالنسبة لإفريقيا والشرق الأوسط وأوروبا. وقال سيمون دي مونتفورت ووكر : «بعد الإطلاق الناجح لمركزنا للبحث والتطوير في الدار البيضاء، يعكس افتتاح مركز أكادير ثقة Oracle في الكفاءات الاستثنائية التي يزخر بها المغرب، وفي طموحاته الرقمية القوية، وفي منظومته المتنامية للابتكار. لقد أصبح المغرب مركزاً تزداد أهميته في مجال الابتكار التكنولوجي، وتوفر أكادير إمكانية الوصول إلى قاعدة ديناميكية من المواهب، من شأنها أن تساعد Oracle على تسريع تطوير تقنيات رائدة في مجالي السحابة والذكاء الاصطناعي، لخدمة العملاء في مختلف أنحاء العالم». وسيضم مركز البحث والتطوير في أكادير فضاءات عمل عصرية قائمة على التعاون، وبيئات تطوير متقدمة، ومختبرات مخصصة للابتكار، صممت لدعم البحث والتجريب وتطوير المنتجات ضمن المحفظة المتنامية لOracle في مجالات تقنيات السحابة والذكاء الاصطناعي. نبذة عن أوراكل توفر أوراكل مجموعات متكاملة من التطبيقات، إلى جانب بنية تحتية آمنة وذاتية التشغيل ضمن Oracle Cloud. للمزيد من المعلومات حول أوراكل، المدرجة في بورصة نيويورك تحت الرمز ORCL، يرجى زيارة الموقع: www.oracle.com . العلامات التجارية أوراكل، وجافا، وMySQL علامات تجارية مسجلة لشركة Oracle Corporation.

title: Find your Whistler feeling: The ultimate six-day itinerary
summary: You know that feeling of pure joy and freedom? When the sun is shining, and you’re fully absorbed in the present moment. That’s summer in Whistler.
body_text: You know that feeling of pure joy and freedom? When the sun is shining, the atmosphere is electric and you’re fully absorbed in the present moment. That’s summer in Whistler. Here, you can soar between mountaintops and paddle over serene water or savor a chef-prepared meal. Whistler delivers summer joy in all forms, whether you're craving an outdoor adventure, cocktails on a sunny patio or a cultural connection. This curated itinerary is your road map to experiencing that Whistler feeling for yourself, with details on how to enter for a chance to win this six-day itinerary next summer. Day 1 – Arrive & Settle into Mountain Life The journey begins as you spot the Coast Mountains and Pacific Ocean from the plane. Touch down at YVR International Airport in Vancouver, recognized as the Best Airport in North America by the Skytrax World Airport Awards. From here, hop on the Whistler Connection service to Whistler, winding north along the scenic Sea-to-Sky Highway. Once you arrive in Whistler, check into the Adara Hotel, a stylish boutique hotel located in the heart of Whistler Village with a rooftop pool. Settle into the rhythms of mountain life with a stroll through the Village, then enjoy dinner at one of the European-inspired eateries owned by the Pare Restaurant Group. You'll be spoiled for choice with Mediterranean comfort food at Caramba!, authentic Italian at Quattro and contemporary French dining at Lorette Brasserie. Day 2 – Adventures From Valley to Peak Spend your first full day in Whistler immersed in the mountains. The Whistler Blackcomb Summer Alpine Experience is a breathtaking gondola and chairlift journey that brings you from the Village to the alpine summit. Ride the record-breaking PEAK 2 PEAK Gondola between Whistler and Blackcomb Mountains, soaring 1,427 feet above Fitzsimmons Creek. Once in the alpine, you'll have access to 30+ miles of hiking trails that bring you to alpine lakes, jutting peaks, and panoramic viewpoints. Be sure to watch for the whistling marmots that gave Whistler Mountain its playful name. After a day of hiking and sightseeing, download to the Village for a taste of local flavors at Alta Bistro. The intimate restaurant is built on farm-to-table dining and has received a host of accolades, including gold at the Vancouver Magazine Restaurant Awards. Indulge in a modern seasonal alpine menu with a curated wine pairing. Day 3 – Lake Lounging & River Paddles In Whistler, the winding rivers and gemlike lakes add to the mystique of this idyllic setting. Cool off from the summer heat with a self-guided paddling tour along the famed River of Golden Dreams, with canoe rentals, life jackets and shuttles provided by family-run Backroads Whistler. The river snakes 3 miles, connecting Alta Lake to Green Lake and is a must-do summer activity for those looking to experience Whistler's natural beauty at a relaxing pace. Wind down in Whistler Village or hang at a lakeside park with views of the mountains. As the sun sets, return to the Village for a one-of-a-kind meal at Teppan Village, where the chefs put on a whimsical show of culinary tricks before plating your Japanese-inspired meal. Day 4 – Culture Meets Valley Bike Rides Spend an entire day taking in nature and culture in Whistler. Begin with a scenic ride on a guided E-Bike Valley Tour with Whistler Eco Tours. Hop in the saddle of a pedal-assisted townie electric bike to ride the Valley Trail with your guide, stopping to take in some of Whistler’s most beautiful lakes, parks, and scenic lookouts. Whistler is pulsing with creativity and has a thriving arts and culture community. Visit the Audain Art Museum, for an exclusive private guided curatorial tour. The museum features a permanent collection that showcases the artistic heritage of British Columbia, bringing in a rotation of exhibits from Canada and around the world. After a day of nature and artwork, spend the evening exploring the vibrant Village before unwinding in the peace of the mountains. Day 5 – Explore the Rugged Backcountry Nestled in the vast Coast Mountain range, Whistler is at the edge of impressive backcountry terrain. Experience the towering peaks and forest valleys that have been carved by ancient volcanoes and glaciers by taking a Side-by-Side Tour with The Adventure Group. Also known as off-road buggies, these backcountry machines are built for rugged terrain, allowing you to splash through rivers and climb steep terrain. After a thrilling tour, take a beat to explore more of Whistler, before ending your day in the renowned Rimrock Café. Unassuming from the outside, this cozy space in Creekside has a passionate following, serving up an upscale menu featuring seafood dishes, expertly prepared me meats and an award-winning wine list. Day 6 – Whistler Village Strolls & Patio Hangs On your final full day in Whistler take time to soak in the Village vibes and celebrate your trip in style. Wander through independent shops, take in local attractions and street art, and explore more lakes and trails. Be sure to stop in for a summer sipper at one of Whistler's many scenic patios, perfect for people watching and taking in the lively energy of Whistler Village. Visit restaurants, bars, and clubs owned by the Gibbons Hospitality Group, where you can use the Gibbons Après Pass for exclusive perks. Day 7 – Departure Day After six days of soaking in the summer feeling of a Whistler stay, it’s time to head home. Take a shared Whistler Connection shuttle transfer to YVR for your return flight home. Inspired by this itinerary? Try it for yourself. Enter the Find Your Whistler Feeling Contest for a chance to experience the ultimate itinerary in Summer 2027 by visiting whistler.com/summer-contest . The grand prize is a six-night trip to Whistler valued at $10,000*: ● Two round-trip flights from a major city to Vancouver, BC ● Round-trip ground transportation from YVR to Whistler with Whistler Connection ● Six nights at Adara Hotel ● Whistler Blackcomb gondola tickets for the PEAK 2 PEAK and Whistler Blackcomb Summer Alpine Experience ● Guided E-Bike Tour with Whistler Eco Tours ● A side-by-side tour with The Adventure Group ● Self-guided paddling from Backroads Whistler ● Guided curatorial tour of Audain Art Museum ● Two complimentary Après Pass memberships from Gibbons Whistler ● Dinners for two at: Alta Bistro , Rimrock Café , Teppan Village and Pare Restaurant Group eateries with the choice of local favorites Caramba! , Quattro or Lorette Brasserie . *Note: This contest is not open to residents of Quebec, New York, Florida and Puerto Rico. title: Polymath Robotics Blog | Meet 2 New Modules: Obstacle Detection + Local Planning
summary: This week, we're introducing 2 more autonomous navigation modules: Obstacle Detection and Local Planning.
body_text: At Polymath Robotics, we make it radically simple to automate off-highway vehicles. We’re releasing 40 autonomous navigation modules over 20 weeks, making it easier than ever to build your off-highway autonomy stack. Each module can be used on its own, or together as a full autonomy solution. This week we’re launching two new modules: Obstacle Detection and Local Planning. ‍ It’s too hard to build autonomous vehicles That’s why we built Polymath Robotics – the autonomous navigation toolkit for off-highway vehicles. Our aim is simple: to streamline the process of automating off-highway vehicles. On average, Polymath reduces the timeline of off-highway autonomy projects by more than a year, or up to 5-10 engineers' worth of effort. With Polymath, you can build off-highway robots without getting mired in complexity. In our effort to simplify automating off-highway vehicles even further, we're unveiling 40 Autonomous Navigation Modules within the next 20 weeks. So far we’ve released 10 different modules! Last week we debuted Remote Emergency Stop ("E-Stop")and Diff Drive Configuration. Today we’re excited to launch our next 2 modules: Obstacle Detection and Local Planning. ‍ Module #11: Obstacle Detection Why we built this: Humans naturally recognize obstacles in their path, but robots need a clear system to distinguish between objects that are "safe" or "unsafe" for interaction. Introducing our Obstacle Detection module – a simple, tuneable framework for your vehicle to identify obstacles nearby. How it works: Obstacle Detection takes raw point clouds and clusters them to identify an “obstacle.” The machine then defines obstacles based on those clusters’ height, distance, and movement. For instance, it won't try to drive over anything taller than one-fourth the height of its wheels. We can adjust these settings for different vehicles and environments. Additionally, we can use machine learning to classify obstacles more accurately when needed. What makes our Obstacle Detection module so powerful? Safer operations: Help your vehicle chart a safer path by detecting obstacles in its way. Flexibility: We can easily tweak the Obstacle Detection parameters, allowing you to change the machine's operational environment without worrying about reprogramming the entire algorithm. Ready out of the box: Obstacle Detection is easy to install as an individual module on your existing autonomy stack, or as part of our full autonomy solution. ‍ Our Obstacle Detection module takes raw point clouds from the vehicle's sensors and clusters them to identify an "obstacle" (in this case, a trash can seen in the camera view on the top left) ‍ Module #12: Local Planning Why we built this: Robots use both global and local planning. Global planning is akin to using Google Maps for directions, while local planning is similar to seeing a bunch of cones in a parking lot and charting a path around them. The problem: Local planning involves making quick decisions in unpredictable settings and can be difficult to develop without consuming excessive computational resources on the machine. That’s why we built the Local Planning module – the easy way to transform raw point cloud data into a unified cost map for efficient, safe robot navigation. How it works: After obstacles are detected, the Local Planning module maps out the optimal path to the destination. It does this by making a "cost map" where obstacles are seen as having a higher cost. Then, it calculates the most direct route that avoids these costly obstacles. Additionally, Local Planning allows you to assign higher costs to specific obstacles like humans, ensuring that the machine maintains a greater distance from them. What makes our Local Planning module so powerful? Mapless navigation: Local Planning does not require pre-mapping of its environment for the machine to navigate safely from A to B. No internet connection needed: Local Planning can find the best path using the computing power onboard the machine, right in its surroundings, without needing an internet connection. Easy to incorporate: like all our modules, you can use Local Planning on its own, or as part of our full autonomous navigation system. ‍ What’s Next Next week, we’ll reveal two more of our 40 Autonomous Navigation Modules. As always, each module easily fits into your existing projects or combines with other Polymath modules to create a complete autonomous navigation system. We’re excited to hear how you plan to use these modules to speed up your off-highway autonomy projects. Contact Sales today. ‍

title: Interoperability: The Future of Smart Appliances
summary: Connected devices are at a crossroads with several challenges OEMs must resolve including interoperability. What is the future of smart appliances?
body_text: Connected Appliances: An Experiment In an April 2018 TED Talk , journalists Kashmir Hill and Surya Mattu shared the results of an experiment on what smart devices know and share about consumers. The main question: once your appliances can talk to you, who else are they going to be talking to? For the experiment, the team transformed Hill’s apartment into a smart home. They connected everything to the internet — the fridge, the television, and even toothbrushes. Mattu installed a special router to examine and analyze network activity for two months. In those two months, there wasn’t a single hour of digital silence in the apartment. Mattu could tell exactly when the family went to bed and woke up, what TV shows they enjoyed watching and for how long, and how often they brushed their teeth. Even when Hill went on vacation for a week with her family, the in-house activity was nonstop. “You give up a little privacy, and you get some convenience or some price breaks in return,” Hill said, adding, “But that wasn’t my experience in my smart home. It wasn’t convenient; it was infuriating.” While she enjoyed amenities like the smart vacuum, other things in the house drove her insane. They ran out of electrical outlets, had to download a dozen apps to control everything, and had to use brand-specific terminology to tell their voice assistant to start the coffee maker. "We need the companies to rethink the design of these devices with our privacy in mind, because we’re not all willing to participate in market research, just because a device we bought has a Wi-Fi connection,” Hill explained. It is easy to assume that consumers relinquish some privacy when purchasing connected devices, but is it fair for them to constantly have their data mined? Even anonymously? This experiment alone displays many of the challenges that solution providers are facing today.
